about.title: About me
about.description: Data engineer with 6+ years of experience at Epsilon France (Publicis Groupe), RiverBank and Corum L'Épargne, on Spark, SQL, Azure Data Factory, BigQuery and Data Vault.
about.lede: Data engineer. I build pipelines that are tested, monitored and built to last.
intro: I'm a data engineer with more than six years of experience designing and running data integration pipelines for companies in finance, insurance, mobility and marketing, as a consultant at Epsilon France (Publicis Groupe) and then as a data engineer at RiverBank and Corum L'Épargne.

I've worked in both worlds: distributed Big Data processing with Spark, Scala and Hadoop, and more traditional platforms built on SQL, Azure Data Factory, Apache NiFi and Google BigQuery. Across them, I focus on what keeps pipelines healthy in production: automated tests, monitoring, data quality and code that the next engineer can maintain.

Today I work on the modern lakehouse stack. I first worked with Data Vault on Corum's data platform; my latest project integrates six European company registers on Databricks and AWS with a medallion architecture, SCD Type 2 history and automated data-quality gates, and I earned the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certification in October 2026.

principles.title: Explicit over implicit
principles.text: Declared schemas instead of inference, configuration instead of copy-paste, and failures that are loud instead of silent.

principles.title: Model for change
principles.text: Sources change their formats and their data. I separate raw history from business rules so a change in one place doesn't break everything downstream.

principles.title: Cost-aware cloud
principles.text: Serverless where it fits, and incremental work where it pays, like geocoding only the addresses that are new.

legal.title: Privacy & legal
legal.description: Privacy notice and legal information for catobyte.co.

sections.title: Privacy
paragraphs: This is a static personal website. It uses no cookies, no analytics, no advertising and no forms, and I don't collect personal data from visitors.

The site is served by Amazon Web Services (Amazon S3 and CloudFront). As with any web host, their servers may process technical data such as your IP address to deliver pages and protect against abuse. I don't use this data to identify visitors.

The interactive map on the project data page loads map tiles from the OpenStreetMap Foundation's tile servers, which receive your IP address and the page address to deliver the tiles. No other page loads content from a third party.

sections.title: External links
paragraphs: Pages may link to external websites such as LinkedIn, GitHub or data publishers. Their own privacy policies apply once you leave this site.

sections.title: Content
paragraphs: Articles and project write-ups reflect my own work and opinions and are provided for informational purposes. Unless stated otherwise, text and images are © Catobyte. You're welcome to share them with a link to the original page.
Datasets described in project pages belong to their publishers and are used under their respective open-data licences.

insights.noscript: The charts and the map on this page are drawn in your browser from the pipeline's published data, so they need JavaScript.
insights.explore_text: Interactive map of every town, fishing hubs, company survival, distress by industry and the data-quality report, refreshed by each pipeline run.

labels.show_table: Show the data as a table
labels.error: The data could not be loaded. Please try again later.
labels.no_activity_codes: no activity code in the published file
labels.jobs_exact_or_low: Exact count, or lower bound of the band

charts.activity_title: Share of active companies that are probably operating
charts.activity_note: Operating = active, minus companies at mass-registration addresses (50+ companies), dormant accounts and pending strike-offs. A company can carry several signals. Dormancy and strike-off are only published by the UK and Irish registers.
charts.hotspots_note: Active companies registered at the same street address. Dormancy and strike-off are only published for the UK.
charts.industry_title: Industry mix: share of each register's active companies
charts.industry_note: NACE Rev. 2 sections, after mapping UK SIC, French NAF, Norwegian SN2007, Irish NACE and Spanish CNAE codes. Sections under 0.5% everywhere are left out.
charts.hubs_title: Fishing hubs: how over-represented fishing is in each town
charts.hubs_note: Location quotient = the town's fishing share divided by its country's. ×200 means fishing is 200 times more common among the town's companies than nationally. Towns with at least {n} active companies.
charts.fishing_jobs_title: Where the fishing and aquaculture jobs are
charts.fishing_jobs_note: Norway publishes exact headcounts per company. France publishes headcount bands, so French areas show the range they imply.
charts.demography_title: Company births and closures per year
charts.demography_note: Registers that list live companies only can't show closures, and their older years are under-counted. {year} is still running and is left out.
charts.survival_title: How many new companies are still alive after 1, 3, 5 and 10 years
charts.survival_note: Only France and Ireland keep closed units with their closure date, which survival analysis needs. A horizon is shown only for cohorts old enough to have reached it.
charts.survival_sections_note: All cohorts since 1980 that are at least five years old. Industries with fewer than 1,000 births are left out.
charts.distress_title: Companies in liquidation, insolvency or pending strike-off, by industry
charts.distress_note: Share of registered companies. France and Navarra publish no such status. Industries with fewer than 1,000 companies are left out.
charts.employment_note_exact: Norway: exact headcounts reported to the register (only part of the units report).
charts.employment_note_bands: Headcount bands: the bar is the lower bound, the lighter part the range up to the band's upper bound.
charts.funnel_title: From raw rows to the map, per register
charts.funnel_note: Bronze keeps every raw row of the latest snapshot (Navarra's file holds nine yearly panels). Silver keeps one current version per company. The bar is the share of silver placed on the map.
charts.precision_title: How precisely each company is placed
charts.precision_note: The most precise tier available wins: address (register coordinates or the geocoding worker), postcode, district, town.
charts.dq_title: Data-quality rules that fired on the latest snapshot
charts.dq_note: Warnings keep the row and are tracked over time. Quarantine moves the row to silver.quarantine with the failed rules. Every other rule passed on every row.
charts.coverage_note: A register is left out of an insight when it doesn't publish the fields needed, so an unknown is never shown as zero. Hover or focus a cell for the reason.

map.status: {n} towns · {total} in total. Circle area is proportional to the count. Click the map to zoom with the wheel.
